name: Sporadic Fatal Insomnia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Sporadic Fatal Insomnia

criteria.description: Progressive and intractable insomnia unresponsive to conventional treatments
Presence of autonomic nervous system dysfunction including hyperhidrosis and tachycardia
Polysomnographic evidence of disrupted sleep architecture with loss of REM and slow-wave sleep
Exclusion of other prion diseases by clinical, laboratory, and genetic testing
MRI or PET evidence of thalamic hypometabolism or atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive intractable insomnia, autonomic dysfunction, and characteristic polysomnographic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires neuropathological confirmation postmortem; genetic testing typically negative for familial mutations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autonomic nervous system hyperactivity (e.g., hyperhidrosis, tachycardia)
searchTerms: excessive sweating and fast heart rate

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe thalamic degeneration leading to disrupted sleep-wake cycle
searchTerms: sleep-wake cycle disturbance from brain damage

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss due to autonomic dysfunction
searchTerms: weight loss due to autonomic issues

laboratory: CSF analysis typically negative for 14-3-3 protein
Elevated CSF tau protein may be present
genetic: No PRNP gene mutations typically found (distinguishing from familial fatal insomnia)
other: Polysomnography revealing loss of slow-wave and REM sleep
Neuropathology shows severe neuronal loss and gliosis in the thalamus

redFlags: Rapidly progressive intractable insomnia unresponsive to treatment
Autonomic instability with hyperhidrosis and tachycardia
Progressive cognitive decline with thalamic dysfunction
references: Montagna P, Gambetti P, Cortelli P, Lugaresi E. Fatal familial insomnia and familial Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease: clinical features and molecular genetics. Brain Pathol. 1998 Jan;8(1):1-11.
Medori R, Tritschler HJ, LeBlanc A, et al. Fatal familial insomnia, a prion disease with a mutation at codon 178 of the prion protein gene. N Engl J Med. 1992 Jun 11;326(7):444-9.
Kong Q, Surewicz WK. Sporadic fatal insomnia: a prion disease associated with thalamic degeneration. Neurology. 2012;79(10):1022-1029.
